title: fix: user-defined frame labels on frame 0 are silently dropped in SWF output
description:
In packages/swf/src/compile.ts, the per-frame FrameLabel (tag 43) emission block (around line 2443) is gated with `if (frameIdx > 0)`, skipping frame 0 to avoid duplicating the scene-name FrameLabel. However, this also silently drops any user-defined named label on frame 0 (e.g., a label named "start" or "menu").

**Bug:** If a layer's frame 0 keyframe has `label = "start"` and `labelType = "name"`, the FrameLabel tag is never emitted. AS2 calls like `gotoAndPlay("start")` or `gotoAndStop("start")` will fail silently.

**Root cause:** The code emits a scene-name FrameLabel unconditionally at the start of each scene (encodeSceneLabel), then skips user labels at frame 0. The correct fix is to emit the scene-name label AND any user-defined label at frame 0, or (better) only emit the scene-name label when multi-scene navigation is needed, and always emit user frame labels regardless of frame index.

**Fix approach:** Within the existing `if (frameIdx > 0)` block, also check frame 0 for user labels, OR change the guard to emit user labels even at frame 0 (the two FrameLabel tags at the same position are legal per SWF spec — Ruffle uses the last one). Alternatively, emit only the user frame label for frame 0 and skip the scene-name label if a user label exists.

**Affected file:** packages/swf/src/compile.ts, around line 2443.
